subject: Geo-segmentation, local compute, and erasure workflow — Dedicated
messages:
From: Claire Dawson <security@finledger.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <infraops@finledger.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Geo-segmentation & erasure expectations for Dedicated deployment

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at FinLedger is excited about the Dedicated option. Before we go further I need to clarify a few items for legal and infra sign-off:

1) If we pin a Dedicated pool to eu-west-1, can you confirm all persistent storage and logs containing customer content will remain in that region (no cross-region backups)?
2) What is Redwood's deletion workflow when we request customer data erasure for a given tenant? We need a documented SLA and auditable evidence.
3) For ephemeral GPU memory / cache (KV cache), do you have any guarantees about leakage to host swap or persistent disks?
4) Can you provide a simple network diagram that shows control-plane interactions from the private customer VPC to Redwood's control plane? We want to map the data flows for our auditors.

Attached are our SOC2 extracts and a short checklist. I appreciate concise, technical answers so our infra/security teams can finish the review.

Regards,
Claire Dawson
Head of Security — FinLedger Inc.
Attachment: SOC2-extracts.pdf (pdf, 320KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Dawson <security@finledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Geo-segmentation & erasure expectations for Dedicated deployment

Hi Claire — thanks for the detailed questions and the SOC extracts. Short answers up front, followed by specifics:

1) Region pinning: Yes — when you provision a Dedicated pool and select eu-west-1 the serving nodes, persistent model caches, and customer-configured object storage endpoints remain in that region. We do not perform automatic cross-region replication for customer content unless explicitly enabled by the customer (e.g., for DR).

2) Deletion workflow & SLA: We offer a documented erasure workflow: a request ticket triggers (a) immediate API-level logical deletion, (b) background scrub of index/KV caches, (c) zeroization of disk blocks and snapshot expiration. SLA for logical deletion request acknowledgement is 24 hours; full completion depends on retention windows and snapshot lifecycle but we publish a 30-day maximum for full physical wipe unless expedited by an erasure-at-rest request (we can provide X days for limited cases). We provide audit logs of the deletion job and a signed statement on completion.

3) Ephemeral caches: KV cache is in-GPU/DRAM and may be spilled to host RAM. We do not write KV cache to persistent disks under normal operation. In exceptional cases (host-level OOM handling) we may use tmpfs, which is mounted on instance local ephemeral storage that is wiped on instance termination. For Dedicated, we ensure instances are provisioned with encrypted ephemeral storage and we document zeroization at termination.

4) Network diagram & control plane: See the attached network diagram draft. Control-plane calls (for deployment orchestration, telemetry, billing) originate from a control subnet in our control plane and use mutually authenticated TLS to your VPC endpoints; customers can opt for all control-plane traffic over a private peering link for extra isolation.

I'll escalate this to our infra team for the formal write-up and an auditable checklist. Marissa — can you produce the formal erasure statement and add the network diagram as a high-res PNG for Claire's auditors? Aditya — please confirm whether we currently keep any long-lived backups outside region for Dedicated customers.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

On Wed, 25 Nov 2026 at 13:10, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I'll escalate this to our infra team for the formal write-up and an auditable checklist. Marissa — can you produce the formal erasure statement and add the network diagram as a high-res PNG for Claire's auditors? Aditya — please confirm whether we currently keep any long-lived backups outside region for Dedicated customers.

Hi Claire — looping in the infra folks and attaching a cropped network diagram (internals only) and the draft erasure statement below. Quick clarifications:

- Backups: For Dedicated customers we do not mirror application data to other regions by default. We do take short-lived snapshots for maintenance; snapshots for eu-west-1 pools are created in eu-west-1. Cross-region backup only occurs if customers enable cross-region DR in their provisioning config.

- Erasure statement (draft):
  * Logical deletion is triggered via API or Console and enters a job queue.
  * We run a job which expunges tenant-specific objects from our metadata DB and marks associated snapshots for expiry.
  * Physical block zeroization is performed on instance termination and on snapshot deletion (cloud provider primitives used where available).
  * We provide an audit package containing timestamps, job IDs, operator IDs, and cryptographic hashes of the deletion event.

Attachment: network-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 620KB)

I'll add the final statement with job IDs once the ticket executes. Claire — would you like the audit package pushed to a secure S3 bucket or delivered as a signed PDF?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Infrastructure PM — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses — this helps. A couple of follow-ups from infra:

- The control-plane over TLS with mTLS for orchestration is acceptable. Please confirm whether control-plane metadata (audit logs) ever include customer PII or content snippets. If so we need to know retention windows and encryption-at-rest details.

- On erasure SLA: the 30-day physical wipe window is understood, but can you confirm an expedited 7-day option in case of regulator requests? We may need an emergency erasure path documented in the contract.

Action items for Redwood:
- Provide the final signed erasure statement with sample audit package (preferred S3 delivery).
- Confirm presence/absence of any cross-region snapshots for eu-west-1 Dedicated pools and add clear wording to the onboarding docs.
- Confirm control-plane audit log fields and retention period.

We will proceed with our internal procurement hold pending those deliverables.

Regards,
Miguel Santos
